mainEntity.name: How does interior log home sealing actually work — is it just caulk in the cracks?

acceptedAnswer.text: The process usually starts with cleaning the interior surfaces, then repairing damaged areas and filling gaps with the right backing and sealant system. For log homes, the goal is a flexible seal that moves with the wood instead of a rigid patch that cracks as the logs shift.
acceptedAnswer.description: It is more than caulk. The job typically involves cleaning, repairing problem areas, and using flexible log-home sealants so the logs can move without reopening the gaps.
